## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** NOMS (National Outcome Measures) assessment data for analysis and reporting. It ingests two raw eInsight exports (child and self-report versions), processes the two-row hierarchical headers, coerces item scores to numeric, filters to the reporting period, pivots to long format (one row per client × item), and pairs each client's initial assessment with their last follow-up more than 3 days after the initial.

**Data sources (eInsight Individual Assessments exports):**

-   **NOMS-child.csv** — Caregiver-completed NOMS for child clients.
-   **NOMS-self_report.csv** — Client self-report NOMS.

Each file has a two-row header: row 1 contains question text, row 2 contains subheader labels (e.g., "Score", "Comments").

**Scoring:** Each item is scored 1–5; values that are non-numeric or outside 1–5 are set to `NA` (and counted). An increase in follow-up score vs. initial indicates a positive outcome. Items are grouped into four domains:

-   Q1: Overall mental health (single item)
-   Q2: Daily life functioning (7 items; domain sum range 7–35)
-   Q3: Well-being (7 items, 3a–3g; domain sum range 7–35). Items 3a–3f ask how often the child felt nervous, hopeless, etc.; 3g asks how much the child was bothered by these problems.
-   Q4: Social connectedness (6 items; domain sum range 6–30)

**Direction:** the outcome logic assumes every item is coded so that higher = better. Q3 items are negatively worded, so this holds only if eInsight codes them in reverse (e.g., "None of the time" = 5). The item-rest check in each section flags any item running the opposite way.

**Room to improve:** a pair whose initial score is already the top of the scale (5) cannot improve. `room_to_improve` flags pairs that can, so % improved can also be reported among them; the share starting at the top changes a lot across cohorts.

The paired output is **item-level** (one row per client × item, each 1–5). Domain sums are not computed here; if domain-level change is needed, aggregate downstream by the item prefix (`q1`, `x2*`, `x3*`, `x4*`).

**Pairing logic:** Rows are grouped by client ID and item. The first assessment is the initial; the last assessment **more than 3 days** after the initial (i.e., ≥4 days) is the follow-up. Clients without a qualifying follow-up are excluded from the paired output.

**Outputs:**

| File | Contents |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `noms_child_pairs_clean.csv` | Long-format paired assessments (one row per client × item), child version |
| `noms_self_pairs_clean.csv` | Long-format paired assessments, self-report version |

-   [ ] The 3-day threshold for "follow-up" is a pragmatic cutoff. Confirm this is the intended definition (code uses `days_since_initial > 3`).
-   [ ] Output is item-level, not domain-level. Confirm downstream analyses (SQ 3.03–3.10) aggregate items into the four domains as intended.
-   [ ] Confirm every item is coded higher = better, especially the Q3 distress items (3a–3g) and Q1. If the item-rest check flags them, their outcome direction must be flipped.
-   [ ] If an item was skipped at the initial assessment, that client × item pair has an `NA` outcome (it does not fall back to a later assessment). The per-item summary reports `n_missing_outcome`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(zoo)

# ---- Configuration: edit paths and reporting window here ----

out_dir <- "/Users/cristin/CWS Dropbox/Cristin Young/CYBHI Project/Rebecca and Tristan and Cristin/EInsight Data"

start_date <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
end_date   <- Sys.Date()   # set to a fixed date (e.g., as.Date("2026-09-30")) to freeze the data window

# Follow-up must be more than this many days after the initial assessment
noms_min_gap_days <- 3

# NOMS item scale
noms_min_score <- 1
noms_max_score <- 5
```

## Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Reads an eInsight assessment CSV export with two-row headers.
# Row 1 holds question text (merged cells export as blanks and are forward-
# filled); row 2 holds sub-headers ("Response", "Score", ...). Returns a data
# frame with combined snake_case names and fully blank columns removed.
# "0" is deliberately NOT treated as missing: it is a valid rating on most tools.
read_assessment_csv <- function(path, na_vals = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A")) {
  raw <- read_csv(path, na = na_vals, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  h1    <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h2    <- unlist(raw[2, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h1_ff <- na.locf(h1, na.rm = FALSE) |> str_squish()

  new_names <- ifelse(
    is.na(h1_ff) | h1_ff == "",
    h2,
    paste(h1_ff, h2, sep = " - ")
  )
  new_names <- janitor::make_clean_names(new_names)

  df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ]
  names(df) <- new_names

  df |> select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))
}

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Converts item columns to numeric. Values that are non-numeric or outside
# [min, max] are set to NA and counted (e.g., a stray "9" or text in a score column).
clean_item_scores <- function(df, cols, min, max, label) {
  num   <- df[cols] |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))
  raw_m <- as.matrix(df[cols])
  num_m <- as.matrix(num)
  n_non_numeric  <- sum(!is.na(raw_m) & is.na(num_m))
  n_out_of_range <- sum(num_m < min | num_m > max, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_non_numeric + n_out_of_range > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_non_numeric, " non-numeric and ", n_out_of_range,
            " out-of-range (", min, "-", max, ") item value(s) set to NA.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item values are numeric and within ", min, "-", max, ".")
  }
  df[cols] <- num |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x < min | .x > max, NA_real_, .x)))
  df
}

# After reverse scoring, every item should correlate positively with the sum of
# the anchor items (excluding itself). Pass the items the instrument never
# reverse-scores as `anchor`: comparing against all items can hide a block of
# reversed items that mostly agree with each other. A negative value means the
# item's direction is wrong (reversed twice, or a positively worded item that
# was not reversed). Returns only the items that need a look (empty = all fine).
item_rest_check <- function(df, cols, label, anchor = cols) {
  anchor_sum <- rowSums(df[anchor], na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- tibble(
    item        = cols,
    item_rest_r = map_dbl(cols, function(col) {
      rest <- anchor_sum - if (col %in% anchor) coalesce(df[[col]], 0) else 0
      suppressWarnings(cor(df[[col]], rest, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    })
  )
  n_neg <- sum(out$item_rest_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_neg, " item(s) correlate negatively with the rest of the scale; ",
            "check reverse scoring (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item-rest correlations are positive.")
  }
  out |> filter(item_rest_r < 0 | is.na(item_rest_r))
}
```

### Score and Pair

Both versions share identical cleaning and pairing logic.

```{r noms-helper}
# Item columns: Q1 plus the numbered sub-items (janitor prefixes names that
# start with a digit with "x", e.g., "2a. ..." -> "x2a_...").
noms_item_pattern <- "^(q1|x).*_score$"

score_and_pair_noms <- function(df, label, expected_items = 21) {
  item_cols <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), noms_item_pattern)]
  if (length(item_cols) != expected_items) {
    warning(label, ": expected ", expected_items, " item columns but found ", length(item_cols),
            ". Check the columns listed below.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  message(label, " item columns: ", paste(item_cols, collapse = ", "))

  items <- df |> clean_item_scores(item_cols, min = noms_min_score, max = noms_max_score, label = label)
  print(item_rest_check(items, item_cols, label))

  scored <- items |>
    mutate(date_completed = parse_einsight_date(date_completed)) |>
    filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date))

  cat(label, "rows after cleaning:", nrow(scored), "\n")
  cat(label, "unique clients:     ", n_distinct(scored$client_system_id), "\n")

  scored |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = all_of(item_cols),
      names_to  = "question",
      values_to = "score"
    ) |>
    group_by(client_system_id, question) |>
    arrange(date_completed, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    mutate(
      days_since_initial = as.integer(date_completed - first(date_completed)),
      initial_date       = first(date_completed),
      initial_score      = first(score)
    ) |>
    filter(days_since_initial > noms_min_gap_days) |>
    slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    transmute(
      client_system_id,
      question,
      initial_date,
      initial_score,
      follow_up_date  = date_completed,
      follow_up_score = score,
      days_since_initial,
      # Higher follow-up = positive outcome (higher score is better)
      # 1 = improved, 0 = no change, -1 = worsened
      positive_outcome = case_when(
        follow_up_score >  initial_score ~ 1L,
        follow_up_score == initial_score ~ 0L,
        follow_up_score <  initial_score ~ -1L
      ),
      score_change      = follow_up_score - initial_score,
      initial_quarter   = paste0("Q", quarter(initial_date),   " ", year(initial_date)),
      follow_up_quarter = paste0("Q", quarter(follow_up_date), " ", year(follow_up_date)),
      # FALSE when the initial score is already at the top of the scale
      room_to_improve   = initial_score < noms_max_score
    )
}

summarise_noms <- function(pairs) {
  pairs |>
    group_by(question) |>
    summarise(
      n_paired          = n(),
      n_improved        = sum(positive_outcome ==  1, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_no_change       = sum(positive_outcome ==  0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_worsened        = sum(positive_outcome == -1, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_improved      = round(100 * n_improved / n_paired, 1),
      n_missing_outcome = sum(is.na(positive_outcome)),
      pct_initial_at_top = round(100 * mean(!room_to_improve, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      pct_improved_room  = round(100 * mean(positive_outcome[room_to_improve %in% TRUE] == 1, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. NOMS Child

```{r noms-child}
noms_child_raw <- read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, "NOMS-child.csv")) |>
  remove_demo_rows("NOMS Child")

pairs_primary_long <- score_and_pair_noms(noms_child_raw, label = "NOMS Child")

cat("NOMS Child paired rows: ", nrow(pairs_primary_long), "\n")
cat("Unique clients paired:  ", n_distinct(pairs_primary_long$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Items covered:          ", n_distinct(pairs_primary_long$question), "\n")

summarise_noms(pairs_primary_long)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. NOMS Self-Report

```{r noms-self}
noms_self_raw <- read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, "NOMS-self_report.csv")) |>
  remove_demo_rows("NOMS Self")

pairs_primary_long_self <- score_and_pair_noms(noms_self_raw, label = "NOMS Self")

cat("NOMS Self paired rows: ", nrow(pairs_primary_long_self), "\n")
cat("Unique clients paired: ", n_distinct(pairs_primary_long_self$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Items covered:         ", n_distinct(pairs_primary_long_self$question), "\n")

summarise_noms(pairs_primary_long_self)
```

write_csv(pairs_primary_long_self, file.path(out_dir, "noms_self_pairs_clean.csv"))

cat("CSVs written successfully.\n")
